fatal_errors: The proposed workflow does not reconstruct the central MTP-plus-free-energy-perturbation intervention and instead trains a generic property surrogate on MD descriptors.

Temperature-ramp NPT simulations can exhibit substantial superheating, hysteresis, and rate dependence, so they do not by themselves provide accurate equilibrium melting temperatures or fusion free energies.
The hypothesis omits the required DFT free-energy reference, MTP-to-DFT energy-difference variance, and validation against thermodynamic integration.
The claimed approximately 5% accuracy and family-wide transferability have no supporting evidence.
Critical electronic-excitation and solid-state short-range-order contributions are absent.
explanation: The response addresses the requested classes of fusion properties and identifies reasonable generic limitations involving force-field and training-set quality. Its experimental falsification test is measurable, although a 5–7% discrepancy would test the asserted accuracy rather than isolate why the method fails. Scientifically, however, it is not the targeted approach: it replaces neither EAM with an MTP as a DFT phase-space surrogate nor TI with FEP, and it provides none of the relevant conditions, benchmark agreement below 0.5 meV/atom, 80% resource saving, electronic 48–57 K shift, or 2.4 meV/atom SRO stabilization. The baseline is also experimental rather than TOR-TILD. With no cited prior evidence and an unreliable direct-ramp route to equilibrium melting, the quantitative performance claim is unsupported.
